item.title: Tokushima Castle Ruins and Mount Bizan — Guide
item.description: Tokushima city grew up around Tokushima Castle, built in the late sixteenth century by the ruling Hachisuka clan at the foot of Mount Bizan. Though the castle buildings are gone, the site is now a pleasant park preserving impressive stone walls and moats, along with the beautiful Senshukaku Japanese landscape garden, a nationally designated scenic spot. Rising directly behind it is Mount Bizan, the symbol of the city, whose summit is reached by a ropeway or a road and rewards you with a sweeping panorama over Tokushima, the Yoshino River delta and the Seto Inland Sea — especially fine at night.

item.title: Shibuya Guide: The Scramble Crossing & Shibuya Sky from Above
item.description: The Shibuya Scramble Crossing is the image that says “Tokyo” more than any other. When the lights turn red in every direction at once, up to 3,000 people surge across from all sides simultaneously beneath a blaze of giant video screens and neon — and somehow nobody collides. It happens again every couple of minutes, all day and late into the night. Watching it, and crossing it yourself, is a rite of passage on any first visit to the city.

item.title: Tokyo Skytree Guide: Tickets, Best Times & What's Worth It
item.description: At 634 metres, Tokyo Skytree is the tallest tower in Japan and the second-tallest structure in the world. From its observation decks, the sheer scale of the Greater Tokyo conurbation — the largest metropolitan area on Earth, home to 37 million people — spreads out in every direction until it dissolves into haze. On a clear day, Mount Fuji floats on the western horizon. It is the definitive “how big is Tokyo, really?
